title: What If You Could Chase a Solar Eclipse for 74 Minutes?
subject: Concorde eclipse

scenes.text: What if you could chase a solar eclipse and make it last more than an hour?
On the ground, the longest totality you can get is about seven minutes.
In 1973, a Concorde took off from the Canary Islands and raced along the Moon's shadow.
The shadow moved at about 1,500 miles an hour. Concorde cruised at 1,350.
At 55,000 feet, seven scientists stayed inside the darkness for 74 minutes.
The shadow was just faster, so it slowly pulled away, and the plane landed in Chad.
